findings.evidence: "The benefits team tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: State budget-tracking ownership once, in one place, and remove the conflicting duplicate statements elsewhere.
findings.violation: This exact responsibility is reassigned to a different office later in the document ("Special Cases" gives it to "the finance liaison," and "Questions and Updates" gives it to "the people operations office"), creating a direct contradiction over who owns this task.

findings.evidence: "the people operations office updates the equipment catalog each quarter. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Consolidate the catalog-update statement into one section and delete the garbled duplicate.
findings.violation: The "Questions and Updates" section repeats this sentence almost verbatim but swaps the subject from "equipment catalog" to "stipend budget," so the date-stamp/audit claim ends up contradicting itself about what is being tracked.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Explicitly name the mechanism, e.g., "the 90-day service requirement" or "the benefit-year claim window."
findings.location: Eligibility, "employees on an approved leave of absence" paragraph
findings.violation: "The stipend clock" is not defined anywhere before this point (no prior clock, timer, or countdown was introduced), so the reader cannot tell what is resuming.

findings.evidence: "Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins" followed later by "the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request."
findings.fix: Lay out the steps as a single numbered sequence so the order of submission, review, and confirmation is unambiguous.
findings.violation: The sequence is contradictory - documents must be submitted before review begins, yet the employee also reviews a summary before submitting the final request, leaving it unclear whether submission or review comes first.

findings.evidence: "The manager reviews the request within two business days." ... "The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: Clarify whether the three-day reminder is a business-day or calendar-day count and how it relates to the two-day review window.
findings.violation: The two timeframes (two business days for review vs. a reminder at three days) are stated independently with no explanation of how they relate, leaving the actual timeline ambiguous.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Reconcile the two sections so there is one authoritative list of required documents.
findings.violation: This contradicts "How to Apply," which requires "the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order" as mandatory items before review - it's unclear whether an original purchase order and physical receipt are actually required or a photo suffices.

findings.evidence: "Additionally, employees shall retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "employees must retain receipts for one year after the purchase date" to match the document's voice.
findings.violation: "Shall" is a legalistic register inconsistent with the "must"/plain-imperative phrasing used everywhere else in the document.

findings.evidence: "The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount."
findings.fix: Add the actual stipend amount or cap, or a reference to where it is published.
findings.violation: A section titled "Reimbursement Amounts" never actually states any dollar figure, percentage, or cap for the stipend, so the core information the section promises is missing.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category."
findings.fix: Break this into separate sentences (one per condition) and either define the annual per-category amount or cite where it is published.
findings.violation: This is a single 90+ word run-on sentence with multiple embedded conditions, and it references "the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes," an amount never defined anywhere in the document.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form... Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person to match the rest of the document, e.g., "The employee records the stipend item..."
findings.violation: This section switches to second-person "you," while the rest of the document consistently uses third person ("employees," "the applicant," "the requester"), an inconsistent voice.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Either expand "Request Steps" to match "How to Apply" in full or remove the redundant section.
findings.violation: This two-step summary omits the manager's approval form and original purchase order that "How to Apply" lists as required, so the two sections describe different, conflicting processes.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Remove this duplicate paragraph or reconcile it with Program Overview so only one office is named as responsible.
findings.violation: This duplicates the Program Overview's sentence almost word-for-word but attributes the budget review to a different party ("finance liaison" vs. "benefits team"), directly contradicting the earlier statement.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout... Once approved, the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle."
findings.fix: Merge this content into the existing process sections rather than repeating it separately.
findings.violation: This section re-describes the intake/approval/payout process already covered by "How to Apply" and "Approval Timeline," adding redundant, only partially consistent detail (e.g., "next pay cycle" is never mentioned in the timeline sections).

findings.evidence: "The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Define what a "repeat request" is and what "escalation" triggers, or remove the sentence if it's out of scope.
findings.violation: "Escalation of repeat requests" is an undefined concept introduced with no prior context - no earlier section discusses repeat requests or what escalation entails.

findings.evidence: "The determination of stipend eligibility happens before any payment goes out."
findings.fix: Rewrite to name the responsible party, e.g., "The benefits team determines stipend eligibility before any payment goes out."
findings.violation: The passive, nominalized phrasing ("the determination... happens") avoids naming who performs the eligibility determination, unlike other sections that name a specific role (manager, finance office, benefits team).

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Delete this duplicate and keep a single, correct statement of who tracks the budget and who date-stamps catalog entries.
findings.violation: This is a third, mutually contradictory restatement of the Program Overview sentence about budget tracking (now a third owner, "people operations office," after "benefits team" and "finance liaison"), and it misapplies the "date stamp" language originally used for catalog entries to budget tracking.
